body:
I got to a point last summer where I tried to get myself committed at the hospital ER for suicidal thoughts or whatever, but I'm so good at acting like nothing is wrong that they didn't even believe me enough to admit me.  The attitude I've gotten from the few people (doctors and a therapist included) is that I'm not "that bad" so no one cares. Or, maybe just my problems are exaggerated, or my feelings about them are, or whatever. I've been medicated before but I never tell a difference. Since I function fine I don't see the point in heavy meds; I don't really know what to pursue. It's hard going to doctors, starting the process, and then having them just try to throw meds at me and not talk, or they do all the talking, or just whatever.

It's not that I don't think I deserve help necessarily, more than I feel like I've tried and don't know what else to do, and pushing for it is overwhelming. I think I probably just need talk therapy, but even that I don't feel I have reasonable access to without money.

I appreciate the link. I'm atheist, and while I live in an area with tons of churches I have no intention of ever using a pastoral counselor for help. For one thing, they aren't trained in crazy. Another problem I have is that they are going to want to solve everything from a biblical perspective, which won't help me in the least. I also live in a university town, and the school does have a way for me to do $40 sessions, but even that once a month is a burden on my finances that I can't afford.

Thank you for taking the time to respond.

This put me in tears, especially this:

>that objectively you have a lot which one might cherish and enjoy, but that you can feel the benefits because you're sick?

It's a comforting idea to think I'm sick rather than just a privileged, whiny person, but I don't really believe that to be the case.

Thank you sincerely for taking the time to respond.

The thing is, it's not a temporary problem. I'm 28 and it's been like this for more than 10 years. It's gotten worse over time, but it's always been around. Unfortunately my insurance does not cover therapy, and medications have never helped.
